# Purchase Agreement form review

**Form reviewed:** Iowa Association of REALTORS® *Iowa Offer to Purchase Real Estate*, 6 pages,
"Updated 3/10/2026" (Copyright 03/2026), generated by Form Simplicity. The agent supplied two blank copies
(an Adobe-only fillable version and a regular PDF version with identical wording), reviewed 2026-10-27.
The printed line numbers let contract wording be cited precisely, e.g. ¶9 TAXES = page 3, lines 101–109.

**Status:** this is a review only. **No property-tax rule has been coded yet.** The method below must first
be checked against a closed transaction's final settlement statement and approved by the agent.

---

## 1. Property taxes — form ¶9, page 3, lines 101–109 (exact wording)

> **TAXES:** All regular taxes due and payable in the fiscal year in which possession is given are to be
> paid by Seller as well as all unpaid taxes that are liens for prior years. All regular taxes for the
> fiscal year in which possession is given (due and payable in the following fiscal year) are to be
> pro-rated between Buyer and Seller as of the date of possession. The basis of such proration shall be
> the taxes that were certified and payable in the prior fiscal year. If such taxes are not based upon a
> full assessment of the present property improvements the proration shall be based on the current
> millage rate and the assessed value for the tax period to date of possession shown on the assessor's
> records, less tax abatement, if any.

### What the wording makes clear

| Topic | What ¶9 says |
|---|---|
| Date that controls | **Possession date**, not closing date. ¶4 says possession is at closing unless agreed otherwise. |
| Fiscal year | Iowa fiscal year, July 1 – June 30. |
| Part A — seller pays in full | Taxes **due and payable** in the fiscal year of possession (the September and March installments of that year), plus any unpaid prior-year tax liens. |
| Part B — prorated | Taxes **for** the fiscal year of possession (billed the *following* year), prorated from July 1 to the possession date. |
| Special case | If the taxes don't reflect a full assessment of current improvements (for example, new construction), a different basis applies: current millage × assessed value, less abatement. |

### What the wording does NOT settle (agent must decide; app will not interpret)

1. **"Prior fiscal year": prior to what?** There are two reasonable readings:
   - **Reading A:** the fiscal year before the possession fiscal year. For an Oct 2026 possession,
     that's the taxes payable Sept 2025 and March 2026.
   - **Reading B:** the most recently certified taxes, i.e. the year before the one the prorated taxes will be
     billed in. For an Oct 2026 possession, that's the taxes payable Sept 2026 and March 2027.
2. **Possession day:** is it a seller day or a buyer day?
3. **Day count:** is the daily rate based on a 365-day year, or the actual days in the fiscal year (366 in a leap year)?
4. **Gross or net taxes:** "Taxes that were certified and payable" doesn't say whether the seller's homestead,
   military, or other credits and exemptions are subtracted first. Note that SF 2472 (2026) replaces the homestead
   credit with a homestead exemption, starting with taxes paid Sept 2027.
5. **When the special-case clause applies:** that's a judgment call for the agent or closing attorney. The app will
   only let you flag it.

### Example (illustration only, made-up numbers)

Possession **Oct 15, 2026** (fiscal year July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027).
Taxes payable Sept 2025 / Mar 2026 = $2,900 per year. Taxes payable Sept 2026 / Mar 2027 = $3,000 per year.

| Line | Reading A | Reading B |
|---|---|---|
| Part A: Sept 2026 installment (usually already paid by seller) | $1,500 if unpaid | same |
| Part A: March 2027 installment (not yet due; seller pays) | $1,500.00 | same |
| Part B: July 1 – Oct 15, 2026 (107 days, possession day counted as seller's) | $2,900 ÷ 365 × 107 = **$850.14** | $3,000 ÷ 365 × 107 = **$879.45** |
| …if the possession day is the buyer's (106 days) | $842.19 | $871.23 |

The closed-transaction test should show which reading and which conventions your closing attorneys actually use.

## 2. Other paragraphs that affect the net sheet

| ¶ | Provision | How the app handles it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purchase price; earnest money | Facts. Earnest money is shown for information only. |
| 3 | Seller pays buyer's brokerage **$___ or ___%**, or "Seller is not being asked to provide compensation" | Separate "seller-paid buyer brokerage" compensation line |
| 4 | Closing "**on or before**" a date; possession at closing unless agreed | Hints under the date fields |
| 5 | Installment contract / assumption / "OTHER" payment terms | Should be flagged for review. Installment contracts change the whole net sheet. |
| 8 | Personal property only by separate bill of sale | Hint; ties into the transfer-tax review flag |
| 9 | Seller pays all special assessments levied or pending, and certified liens; holdback escrow for preliminary/deficiency assessments; seller pays utilities/trash/sewer attributable to their ownership | Optional cost lines, including "Escrow holdback for pending / deficiency assessments" |
| 9 | Interest, insurance, HOA dues, **unused fuels at current market value**, land leases, rents prorated to **possession** | Optional lines: "Unused fuel / propane" credit, HOA, rent / security deposits. Entered manually; no proration math yet. |
| 10 | Casualty before closing: buyer may close and get a credit for the seller's insurance deductible | Rare; add as a custom line if it happens |
| 13 | Inspection: seller may cure, negotiate, or decline | Repairs and credits go in as custom lines |
| 14 | Septic inspection by addendum | Optional "Septic time-of-transfer inspection" line |
| 15 | Wood pest inspection at buyer's **or seller's** expense; treatment at seller's option | Optional "Wood pest inspection / treatment" line |
| 18 | Seller provides abstract continued to within 30 days of closing; conveys by warranty deed | Abstract continuation and deed preparation lines (already separate) |
| 26 | Typed or handwritten provisions override printed ones | A future AI reader must give ¶29 and addenda priority |
| 29 | "Other provisions" | **The likely place for seller-paid closing costs and concessions.** The form has no printed blank for them. |
| — | **Transfer tax is not mentioned** | Iowa Code §428A makes the seller (grantor) liable. The app includes it as a seller cost, and you can switch it off. |

## 3. Technical note about the files

The first copy supplied is an Adobe "XFA" fillable form. Browsers and most PDF tools display only a page
saying "requires Adobe Reader." The app now warns about this when such a file is uploaded. The signed copy exported from your
e-signature or forms system will usually be an ordinary PDF that displays and reads normally. The second copy
supplied (a regular PDF) displays and reads correctly, including its printed line numbers. A future contract
reader can cite page and line for every value it suggests.
